<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_
- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX), try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX), try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX), try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX), try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via connector_action (literal, a string literal in INLINE_CALLOUT_FIX), try_catch (literal, a string literal in scanAfterSaveInlineRetry; a string literal in validateAfterSaveInlineRetry))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21667430198863ce947f31cce4b37d14650425a0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0b2a1b9de037c834ebc792bf9b7afba9a6734275` — the merge of head `217d1e884d7fad075d2586936901fb10697e5825` into base `21667430198863ce947f31cce4b37d14650425a0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0b2a1b9de037c834ebc792bf9b7afba9a6734275 && git checkout 0b2a1b9de037c834ebc792bf9b7afba9a6734275
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 21667430198863ce947f31cce4b37d14650425a0 217d1e884d7fad075d2586936901fb10697e5825 && git checkout -B drift-repro 21667430198863ce947f31cce4b37d14650425a0 && git merge --no-ff 217d1e884d7fad075d2586936901fb10697e5825

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21667430198863ce947f31cce4b37d14650425a0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 21667430198863ce947f31cce4b37d14650425a0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b8376417f0e2dd055bcf407c434a785df4c4f14`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts (evidence); .changeset/32161-after-save-inline-retry-refused.md, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/automation.json (prose and semver)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; `record-recognisers --template --paths` answers that the paths decide no face and the changeset's line decides). Inputs: card #32161 body and all 9 comments, PR #32515 body, file list (12 files) and net diff, check-runs on the head. Cited code read on `origin/main` `1ff9f80d` (merge base `463b8ea5`), never reviewed: `record-change-trigger.ts`, `engine.ts` (`retryExecution`, the trigger callback), `builtin/try-catch-node.ts`, `builtin/http-nodes.ts`, `builtin/connector-nodes.ts`, `plugin-extension-api.ts` (`deriveTriggerBinding`), `spec/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts`, `spec/automation/region-slots.ts`, `spec/shared/retry-policy.zod.ts`, `lint/flow-walk.ts`, `lint/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts`.

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-11-12T03:13:53Z: 72 runs, 60 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 running (at 03:12:16Z `Test Core (7/8)` was still running; it ended `success`). Among them: Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint lane, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger), Test Core 1 to 8 of 8, Test UI 1 to 16 of 16, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Build Docs, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard.

### ① Derived judgments

What the diff refuses, read from the tree: a flow whose first `start` node carries a string `config.triggerType` matching `^record-after-(create|insert|update|delete|write)$`, and which holds an `http` node without `config.durable === true`, or a `connector_action` node, inside (a) the `try` region of a `try_catch` whose `retry.maxRetries` is at least 1, at any region depth below it, or (b) anywhere in a flow whose `errorHandling.strategy` is `'retry'`.

- **After a record change is judged by the trigger's own grammar: right.** `triggerTypeToHookEvents` maps exactly `record-(before|after)-(create|insert|update|delete|write)`; the PR's regex is its after-phase half, so after-insert, after-delete and the `write` union are all judged, and `record-before-*` is not. The only route to the `record_change` kind is a string start-node `triggerType` (`resolveFlowTriggerKind`); the array form binds no hook and is rightly not judged.
- **The save does wait: right.** The hook handler `await callback(automationCtx)`; the engine's callback returns the run's promise; `try-catch-node.ts` and `retryExecution` both `await` a `setTimeout` per attempt inline.
- **Retry sources are complete for the builtins: right.** No node-level retry exists: `supportsRetry` is a descriptor flag nothing reads, the `http` node has no retry of its own, and `connector_action` awaits the handler once.
- **`durable` is read as the node reads it: right.** `http-nodes.ts` takes the outbox arm on `cfg.durable === true`, the same strict test both judges use.
- **Every publish door: right.** The engine check sits in `registrationChecks`, so it rides `registerFlow` (POST /automation, clone, and the boot bind, whose `try`/`catch` in `plugin.ts` keeps the kernel up). The lint rule sits in the gating `lintFlowPatterns`, which reaches the metadata save and publish doors and `os validate` / `build` / `lint`. The integration test pins the boot bind (kernel `running`, flow not armed, the read serves the stored body with `registration.state: refused` and the reason), the save door's `422 INVALID_METADATA` carrying the rule, the draft's `_diagnostics`, and a durable control that is armed. A refused stored row reads as refused; it does not vanish.
- **Not refused, each checked against the code:** a `durable: true` http node (pinned); a before-trigger, a scheduled and a manual flow (pinned); an api or time-relative flow (the regex cannot match; not pinned); an http node no retry reaches, `maxRetries: 0`, and a node in the `catch` region of the retrying `try_catch` (pinned); a `subflow` callee (not walked, declared).
- **Newly refused though harmless or only conservatively harmful, named so the seat owns them:**
  - an `http` node inside an inner `try_catch` that catches its failure, itself inside a retried outer `try` (or under the flow-level retry): the outer retry never fires on that node's failure, but re-runs it when a later sibling fails. The rule reads "a retry reaches it", not "its failure is retried". Right as a conservative reading; the prose says "reaches".
  - a retry with `backoffMs: 0` and `maxRetries: 1`: refused by shape, though the hold is one extra call.
  - a `connector_action` whose connector answers in process: refused under a retry all the same; the message says "calls an outside system".
  - a flow that is switched off: `activateFlowTrigger` never arms it, yet both judges refuse it. Same as every other registration check (the start-less precedent #32273 / #32340).
- **One escape, both judges agreeing with each other and not with the trigger: wrong, should-fix (④ F1).** The trigger trims the token before matching; neither new judge does.
- **Ruling scope: met, not exceeded.** Ruling 6810500711 asks for the refusal of an inline retrying http node in after-record-change flows, tells step 0 to measure which nodes call out "so the refusal covers exactly them", and wants the showcase flow changed in the same PR. `connector_action` is that measurement's answer (claim amendment item 2). The lint door is the precedent's (#32340) way of making "at publish" true at the metadata save door (amendment item 1). The ruling's interim (C's shorter default ladder) is not implemented because it has no object; see ③.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: right.** `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/lint` take `minor`. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: the level follows the kind alone, a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING by its banner, not by a `major` bump. The changeset carries the `!` title, the **BREAKING** paragraph, both declaration lines, the before / now / not-judged account, the author's fix per node type, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no key is added, removed or renamed, and no rewrite keeps the author's meaning). `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `check:adr-0087-registration`) are `success` on the head.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: right.** A flow body every door accepted is now refused, a tightened requirement on what an author can write; the lint export and the explanation entry are additive and are named on the same line.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`: legitimately out of this PR.** The `http` row (line 94) and the `try_catch` row (line 73) on `main` stay true after this PR; they omit the new restriction, they do not contradict it, so the claim's "sentences this PR makes false" allowance does not reach them. The claim template lets a PR outside `domain:skills` teach in the docs and owe the skill (`skills/**` only on `domain:skills` PRs). ⛔ Owed by the seat before ACCEPT: file the card and rewrite `owed — FILES` to `#N` on the PR body.
- **One overstatement in shipped prose: should-fix (④ F2).** The changeset title says "so a record save never waits through a retry ladder".

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, branch `claude/project-thread-rks6pq` (the claim's measured platform exception to the branch name). Every deviation in os-dev-report 6813188548:

1. **`packages/lint/**` added to the file surface.** Answered: claim amendment 6811718614 item 1, precedent #32340; the diff stays inside the rule, its explanation entry, its export and its tests.
2. **`connector_action` refused beside `http`.** Answered: amendment item 2; verified in `connector-nodes.ts` (the handler is awaited inline, no background arm).
3. **No default-ladder change (the ruling's interim).** Answered on the facts: `retryPolicyShape().maxRetries` is `.default(0)` (`retry-policy.zod.ts` line 104), `strategy: 'retry'` without a count is refused, and the http node has no retry of its own, so there is no default ladder to shorten. ⚠ Escalated all the same: the maintainer's 「同意」 covered "D with C's interim". The seat's release sentence to the maintainer must say that half was found to have no object, beside the BREAKING consent the PR body already asks for.
4. **`showcase_project_escalation` changed too; `showcase_resilient_sync` made on-demand instead of durable.** Answered: both lie in the claimed `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/**`; the first is forced by the rule; the second departs from the analysis' "change one config", and is the better call, since a durable push would never fail in the run and the P1 item `automation.flow-error-handling` needs the deterministic handled failure.
5. **`validating-metadata.mdx` matrix row.** Answered: a new row, not a sentence made false, so strictly past the claim's wording; the docs drift check asked for it and it is accurate. Accepted as gate-required.
6. **`flows.mdx` paragraph** (not listed by the dev as a deviation): also a new paragraph, not a corrected sentence. It is what the `Skills-docs:` line cites as "taught here". Accepted on the same ground.
7. **PR-body trailer** (the signed HTML comment as the last line). Answered: relay mechanics; `PR-body guards` is `success` on the head.
8. **`out_of_scope_findings`: the subflow-callee hole, "noted, not filed".** Escalated to the seat: it is a declared gap in the ruling's stated outcome, so it needs a card or a recorded decision not to file, together with F2 below.

Not the reviewer's to give: the BREAKING consent. The PR is a draft and asks the maintainer whether the ruling's 「同意」 counts.

### ④ Design judgment

**`flow-registration-checks.ts` (`validateAfterSaveInlineRetry`).** Holds against the code it reads. The walk uses the spec's `FLOW_REGION_SLOTS_BY_TYPE` (loop `body`, parallel `branches`, try_catch `try` / `catch`), so nesting depth is unbounded and a node in a loop inside a retried `try` is found (pinned). `retriedBy` is inherited downward and set only on the `try` slot, so a `catch` region is judged by what encloses the `try_catch`, not by its own retry: the catch of a retrying `try_catch` is clean (pinned), and the same catch under a flow-level retry is refused, which is right because `retryExecution` re-runs the whole flow. One refusal per flow lists every node; the message names the node, the retry source, the token and the node type's fix, and each sentence is true of the code.

**`lint-flow-patterns.ts` (`scanAfterSaveInlineRetry`).** The same predicate over raw records: same regex, same two node types, same strict `durable === true`, same slot table through `ownRegionKeys`. I found no flow that one judge refuses and the other accepts within what the schema admits.

**Findings.**

- **F1 · should-fix · a trailing-whitespace token escapes both judges.** `triggerTypeToHookEvents` matches `triggerType.trim()`, and lint's `flow-trigger-unknown-event` tests the trimmed token too, so `'record-after-update '` passes the token rule, binds `afterUpdate`, and holds the save, while `AFTER_RECORD_CHANGE_TRIGGER.test(triggerType)` in both new judges answers false. The judges agree with each other and disagree with the trigger they cite. Fix: trim in both, with one pin each. Not a must-fix: it takes a malformed token no picker writes, and nothing harmless is refused.
- **F2 · should-fix · "the save no longer waits" is not unconditional, and three published sentences say it is.** `http-nodes.ts`: with `durable: true` and no messaging HTTP outbox wired, the node logs and falls back to the inline fetch. Inside a retried `try` that is the refused shape again, accepted, with the full ladder on the save's path. The PR body's Acceptance notes say so; the engine fix text, the lint hint, `flows.mdx`, the `os explain` entry and the changeset ("never waits through a retry ladder") do not. The ruling prescribes this fix and the fallback is existing behaviour outside the diff, so this is no must-fix. Owed: one clause in the changeset and the docs paragraph naming the no-outbox fallback, and a card for the residue (this and the subflow callee of ③ item 8).
- **F3 · should-fix · the `connector_action` fix offers a route the platform's own guidance closes.** "send the call through an `http` node with `durable: true`": a connector is how a flow calls with a credential, and `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` line 94 says an http node's `url` and `headers` are served as written and must never hold one (lint's `flow-credential-literal`). For an authenticated connector only "remove the retry" (or run on demand or on a schedule) is open. Say so in the fix text, the hint and the explain entry, so an AI author is not steered to a credential literal.
- **F4 · nit · two hand-kept copies.** The token regex and the node-type-to-fix map exist once in `service-automation` and once in `lint`, bound only by mirrored test cases. No parity pin; `packages/spec` was outside the claim.
- **F5 · nit · depth.** Lint stops at `MAX_REGION_DEPTH` (16) and the engine does not, so a flow nested deeper than 16 regions would save and then read refused. Unreachable in any reviewable flow.
- **F6 · nit · pins.** The `it.each` lists four tokens; `record-after-insert` is in the regex and unpinned, and no control pins an `api` flow or the catch region under a flow-level retry.
- **F7 · nit · checklist bookkeeping.** `automation.flow-node-type-matrix` revision 14's history row says "fixtures.requires' record_change chain"; the sentence changed is `steps[2]`, and `fixtures.requires[0]` (the node-type map) is unchanged, as the row's last sentence says.

**`rule-explanations.ts`, `index.ts`.** The entry is registered and exported; its paragraphs match the code, subject to F2 and F3.

**`examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts`.**
- `showcase_resilient_sync`: a bare start node, two input variables, and the three `record.*` reads re-pointed to `taskId` / `title`. The try region, the retry ladder (`maxRetries: 3`) and the catch region's write of `sync_status` / `sync_error` are unchanged, so `automation.flow-error-handling` keeps its fixture: step 1 fires it on demand, acceptance[2] still reads `retryAttempt` 0 to 3, and step 3 still re-reads the task its `taskId` names. The other references at the head (`coverage.ts`, `task.object.ts`, the node-type map row `try_catch=showcase_resilient_sync`) stay true.
- `showcase_project_escalation`: the push is `durable: true` and the `retry` is gone; the comment's claim (the try region fails only when the request cannot be queued) matches the durable arm's `failed to enqueue` return. No test or checklist sentence at the head depends on the catch region running.
- Showcase tests and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are `success` on the head.

**Checklist.** Three items bumped by one with a dated history row each (13 to 14, 6 to 7, 13 to 14); each changed sentence is true of the head; each row says it was read from code and not re-driven live. Only F7 is off.

**Docs.** The `flows.mdx` paragraph and the matrix row state the rule as the code has it, subject to F2 and F3. No sample in `content/docs` or `skills` combines an after-trigger, a retry and an outbound node, so no example is left teaching the refused shape.

No must-fix. No security item.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-rks6pq`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CaP1iy4RSEQbW6177G`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `217d1e884d7fad075d2586936901fb10697e5825`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts (evidence); .changeset/32161-after-save-inline-retry-refused.md, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/automation.json (prose and semver)

Delta round over record 6813326147 (PASS at `2b8376417f0e2dd055bcf407c434a785df4c4f14`; should-fix F1 to F3, nits F4 to F7). Face unchanged: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, BREAKING). The delta `2b837641..217d1e88` is one commit, `217d1e88` "act on the contract review", 9 files, +65 −29; no commit of `main` is in it and the merge base is still `463b8ea5`. Inputs: card #32161 body and its 9 comments (none newer than the dev report 6813188548), PR #32515 body as patched by the seat and its 2 comments, the delta diff, and the net diff where the delta touches it. Cited code read at the head, never reviewed: `trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts` (`triggerTypeToHookEvents`), `spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts` (`resolveFlowTriggerKind`), `service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.ts`, `lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts`. Follow-up cards #32525 and #32526 read (both open, filed 2026-11-12T03:17Z).

Check-runs on the head: read at 2026-11-12T03:32:01Z (48 runs, 23 still running), 03:36:50Z (69 runs, 30 running), 03:47:06Z (16 running) and, final, 2026-11-12T03:57:06Z: 72 runs, 60 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 running. Among them: Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint lane, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger), Test Core 1 to 8 of 8 and its roll-up, Test UI 1 to 16 of 16, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Build Docs, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard. The head was still `217d1e88` at the final read.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The accept set moves by one thing only: a start-node token with blanks around it.** Both judges now test `triggerType.trim()` against the unchanged `^record-after-(create|insert|update|delete|write)$`.
